prompt: A $45°$-$45°$-$90°$ triangle has legs of length $7$. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
hint: The sides of a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle are in the ratio $1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}$.

hints.text: The sides of a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle are in the ratio $1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}$.
The hypotenuse is the leg times $\sqrt{2}$.

explanation: In a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle the two legs are equal and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{2}$ times a leg.

alternativeExplanations.title: The two special triangles
steps: $45$-$45$-$90$: sides $1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}$, an isosceles right triangle — half a square along its diagonal.
$30$-$60$-$90$: sides $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, with the shortest side opposite the $30°$ — half an equilateral triangle.
Choice C uses the wrong triangle's radical, which is why both appear among the choices.
